headline: The evidence is inconclusive: no clear change in Nilgiris downpours
summary: None of the three rain measures shows a clear trend over 1981–2025.
verdict: Heavy-rain days, the wettest day of each year and total yearly rain show no clear trend. Total rain edges up (+45 mm per decade) but could be chance (p = 0.15).

evidence_notes.heavy_days: No change in heavy-rain days. This data averages rain over a ~50 km grid, which smooths out extreme days, especially in hills where rain changes from one slope to the next.
evidence_notes.max_day: The wettest day of each year shows no clear change.
evidence_notes.total: Total yearly rain edges up, but not clearly enough to call.

devils_advocate: A ~50 km grid spans both the wet western slopes and the drier eastern side of the hills, and blends satellite and model inputs, so local extremes are averaged away.
devils_advocate_note: We keep this objection on the record.
can_say: Rain in the Nilgiris region shows no clear long-term change in this data.
what_data_cannot_tell_us: Whether the downpours that trigger landslides on particular slopes are becoming more common.
would_change_it: Rain-gauge records from stations across the hills.
next_witness: India Meteorological Department station data for the Nilgiris.
